 **Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.

+**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
+
 **Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
 _Avoid_: converged
 
 **Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
 
+**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
+
 **Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
 _Aliases_: KF
 
@@ -62,6 +66,10 @@ ## Language
 
 **Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
 
+**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
+
+**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
+
 **Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
 
 **Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

30	#
31	# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
32	# files (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock
33	# files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) and without binaries.
34	#
35	# Label rule: a feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit
36	# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
37	# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
38	# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
39	# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
40	# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
41	# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
42	# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
43	# in a fixture file (source fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>); the grader uses them
44	# only for refuted share. Titles are control-stripped, capped at 160 chars,
45	# and a title matching a secret pattern drops its finding; every written
46	# file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails.
47	#
48	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 refused / spec error / secret found / check failed, 2 usage
49	# Tested by evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats.
50	# =============================================================================
51	set -euo pipefail
52	export LC_ALL=C
53	
54	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
55	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
56	
57	exec python3 -I - "$REPO_ROOT" "$@" <<'PY'
58	import argparse, csv, hashlib, io, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
59	
60	HARNESS_ROOT = sys.argv[1]
61	argv = sys.argv[2:]
62	
63	ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="seed-corpus-from-record.sh", add_help=True)
64	ap.add_argument("sprint", nargs="?")
65	ap.add_argument("record_ref", nargs="?")
66	ap.add_argument("--out"); ap.add_argument("--base"); ap.add_argument("--head"); ap.add_argument("--fix")
67	ap.add_argument("--feedback"); ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
68	ap.add_argument("--build-manifest", metavar="FIXTURE"); ap.add_argument("--approve", metavar="FIXTURE")
69	ap.add_argument("--by"); ap.add_argument("--freeze", action="store_true"); ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
70	ap.add_argument("--repo", default=HARNESS_ROOT)
71	ap.add_argument("--corpus", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "fixtures", "review-prs"))
72	ap.add_argument("--tasks-dir", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "tasks"))
73	try:
74	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
75	except SystemExit as e:
76	    sys.exit(2 if e.code else 0)
77	
78	REPO, CORPUS = os.path.abspath(args.repo), os.path.abspath(args.corpus)
79	NO_SECRETS = os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "graders", "no-secrets.sh")
80	LABELS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "labels")
81	MANIFESTS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "manifests")
82	FX_RX = re.compile(r"^pr-[0-9]{2}$")
83	HEADER = ["defect_id", "severity", "category", "file", "must_match", "label_source", "source"]
84	
85	def fail(msg, code=1):
86	    print(f"seed-corpus: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
87	    sys.exit(code)
88	
89	def git(*a, binary=False, check=True):
90	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, *a], capture_output=True, text=not binary)
91	    if check and p.returncode != 0:
92	        fail(f"git {' '.join(a[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr if not binary else p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')).strip()[:300]}")
93	    return p.stdout
94	
95	def rev(r):
96	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{r}^{{commit}}"], capture_output=True, text=True)
97	    if p.returncode != 0:
98	        fail(f"missing commit: {r}")
99	    return p.stdout.strip()
100	
101	def show(r, path):
102	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "show", f"{r}:{path}"], capture_output=True)
103	    return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else None
104	
105	CTRL = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f  ]")
106	def clean(s, cap=160):
107	    s = CTRL.sub(" ", s)
108	    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
109	    return s if len(s) <= cap else s[: cap - 1].rstrip() + "…"
110	
111	SECRET_RX = [re.compile(p) for p in (
112	    r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}", r"sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}", r"ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}", r"gho_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}",
113	    r"glpat-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}", r"xox[bpors]-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+", r"sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}",
114	    r"password\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}", r"secret\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}")]
115	def has_secret(s):
116	    return any(r.search(s) for r in SECRET_RX)
117	
118	REDACTED = [0]
119	def redact(b, count=True):
120	    """Secret-shaped strings in verbatim copies of tracked files (fake test keys)
121	    become a fixed marker, identically in base/, head/ and head.diff; line
122	    numbers never move. Counted in the dropped report."""
123	    if b is None:
124	        return None
125	    t = b.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(b, bytes) else b
126	    for r in SECRET_RX:
127	        t, n = r.subn("REDACTED-TEST-SECRET", t)
128	        REDACTED[0] += n if count else 0
129	    return t.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(b, bytes) else t
130	
131	def sha(path):
132	    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
133	
134	def freeze():
135	    entries = []
136	    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
137	        for f in files:
138	            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
139	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS":
140	                entries.append(rel)
141	    lines = [f"{sha(os.path.join(CORPUS, rel))}  {rel}" for rel in sorted(entries)]
142	    open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
143	    return len(lines)
144	
145	def check():
146	    bad, n = [], 0
147	    for line in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8"):
148	        if not line.strip():
149	            continue
150	        n += 1
151	        d, rel = line.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)
152	        p = os.path.join(CORPUS, rel)
153	        if not os.path.isfile(p) or sha(p) != d:
154	            bad.append(rel)
155	    listed = {l.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)[1] for l in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}
156	    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
157	        for f in files:
158	            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
159	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS" and rel not in listed:
160	                bad.append(rel + " (not listed)")
161	    if bad:
162	        fail("SHA256SUMS mismatch: " + ", ".join(bad[:20]))
163	    print(f"corpus OK: {n} files match SHA256SUMS")
164	
165	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- labels I/O
166	def read_labels(fx):
167	    path = os.path.join(LABELS_DIR, f"{fx}.tsv")
168	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
169	        fail(f"labels not found: {path}")
170	    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
171	    if not text or not re.match(r"^# approved-by: \S", text[0]):
172	        fail(f"{path}: the first line must be '# approved-by: <who> <date>' (or 'pending')")
173	    approved_by = text[0][len("# approved-by: "):].strip()
174	    body = [l for l in text[1:] if l and not l.startswith("#")]
175	    if not body or body[0].split("\t") != HEADER:
176	        fail(f"{path}: header must be: " + "\t".join(HEADER))
177	    rows = []
178	    for i, l in enumerate(body[1:], 2):
179	        cells = l.split("\t")
180	        if len(cells) != len(HEADER):
181	            fail(f"{path}: row {i} has {len(cells)} columns, want {len(HEADER)}")
182	        rows.append(dict(zip(HEADER, cells)))
183	    return approved_by, rows, text
184	
185	def unique_line(lines, needle):
186	    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1) if needle in l]
187	    return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None
188	
189	def build_manifest(fx):
190	    approved_by, rows, _ = read_labels(fx)
191	    fyaml = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "fixture.yaml")
192	    meta = {}
193	    for l in open(fyaml, encoding="utf-8"):
194	        m = re.match(r"^(sprint|head_commit|fix_commit|record_ref):\s*\"?([^\"\n]*)\"?$", l)
195	        if m:
196	            meta[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
197	    defects, regions, errors, order = {}, [], [], []
198	    for r in rows:
199	        if r["label_source"] not in ("review", "audit", "bridgebuilder", "fix"):
200	            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: label_source {r['label_source']!r}"); continue
201	        hp = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "head", r["file"])
202	        if not os.path.isfile(hp):
203	            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: head/{r['file']} missing"); continue
204	        lines = open(hp, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().splitlines()
205	        if r["label_source"] == "fix":
206	            m = re.match(r"^fix/[0-9a-f]+:(\d+)-(\d+)$", r["source"])
207	            if not m:
208	                errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: fix source must be fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>"); continue
209	            regions.append({"id": r["defect_id"], "file": r["file"], "start": int(m.group(1)), "end": int(m.group(2)),
210	                            "source": r["source"]})
211	            continue
212	        at = unique_line(lines, r["must_match"])
213	        if at is None:
214	            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: must_match {r['must_match']!r} is not on exactly one line of head/{r['file']}"); continue
215	        d = defects.get(r["defect_id"])
216	        if d is None:
217	            order.append(r["defect_id"])
218	            defects[r["defect_id"]] = {"id": r["defect_id"], "file": r["file"], "anchor_line": at, "anchors": [at],
219	                                       "must_match": r["must_match"], "severity": r["severity"], "category": r["category"],
220	                                       "label_source": r["label_source"], "source": r["source"],
221	                                       "source_commit": meta.get("head_commit", "")[:8], "synthetic": False}
222	        else:
223	            if d["file"] != r["file"]:
224	                errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: extra anchor rows must name the same file"); continue
225	            d["anchors"].append(at)
226	    if errors:
227	        fail(f"{fx}: " + "; ".join(errors))
228	    out = []
229	    for k in order:
230	        d = defects[k]
231	        d["anchors"] = sorted(set(d["anchors"]))
232	        if len(d["anchors"]) == 1:
233	            del d["anchors"]
234	        out.append(d)
235	    man = {"fixture": fx, "approved": approved_by != "pending", "approved_by": approved_by,
236	           "record": {"sprint": meta.get("sprint"), "record_ref": meta.get("record_ref"),
237	                      "head_commit": meta.get("head_commit"), "fix_commit": meta.get("fix_commit")},
238	           "defects": out, "fix_regions": regions}
239	    os.makedirs(MANIFESTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
240	    json.dump(man, open(os.path.join(MANIFESTS_DIR, f"{fx}.json"), "w"), indent=2)
241	    return man
242	
243	# ------------------------------------------------------------ simple modes
244	if args.check:
245	    check(); sys.exit(0)
246	if args.freeze:
247	    print(f"froze {freeze()} files in SHA256SUMS"); sys.exit(0)
248	if args.build_manifest:
249	    if not FX_RX.match(args.build_manifest):
250	        fail("fixture id must be pr-NN", 2)
251	    m = build_manifest(args.build_manifest)
252	    n = freeze()
253	    print(f"{args.build_manifest}: {len(m['defects'])} label(s), {len(m['fix_regions'])} fix region(s); approved={m['approved']}; SHA256SUMS {n} files")
254	    sys.exit(0)
255	if args.approve:
256	    fx = args.approve
257	    if not FX_RX.match(fx) or not args.by or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9 ._@-]{3,80}$", args.by):
258	        fail("--approve pr-NN needs --by '<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>' (letters, digits, space . _ @ -)", 2)
259	    path = os.path.join(LABELS_DIR, f"{fx}.tsv")
260	    _, _, text = read_labels(fx)
261	    text[0] = f"# approved-by: {args.by}"
262	    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(text) + "\n")
263	    m = build_manifest(fx)
264	    freeze()
265	    print(f"{fx}: approved by {args.by}; {len(m['defects'])} label(s)")
266	    sys.exit(0)
267	
268	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- seed
269	if not args.sprint or not re.match(r"^[0-9]{1,5}$", args.sprint or ""):
270	    fail("usage: seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [...] (see --help)", 2)
271	if not args.record_ref or not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$", args.record_ref):
272	    fail("a record ref is required (e.g. origin/record/cycle-128-a2a)", 2)
273	sprint = args.sprint

278	    for r in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines)), delimiter="\t", quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE):

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}

   283	# The suite-level STATUS.json merges every batch: counters add per arm; the
   284	# state is failed > running > partial > complete; source/model must agree.
   285	aggregate_status() {
   286	  local agg="$SUITE_DIR/STATUS.json" lockd="$SUITE_DIR/.status.lock" n=0
   287	  until mkdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null; do n=$((n + 1)); [[ $n -gt 50 ]] && return 0; sleep 0.1; done

   291	    (map(.state) | max_by(rank)) as $state |
   292	    {schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, state: $state,
   293	     batches: map({batch, state, started, finished}),
   294	     per_arm: (reduce (.[] | .per_arm | to_entries[]) as $e ({};
   295	        .[$e.key] |= {trials_done: ((.trials_done // 0) + $e.value.trials_done),
   296	                      trials_failed: ((.trials_failed // 0) + $e.value.trials_failed),
   297	                      trials_planned: ((.trials_planned // 0) + $e.value.trials_planned)})),
   298	     source_commit: (map(.source_commit) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   299	     model_id: (map(.model_id) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   300	     started: (map(.started) | min), finished: (if $state == "running" then null else (map(.finished) | max) end)}' \
   301	    $(find "$SUITE_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name STATUS.json | sort) > "$agg.tmp" 2>/dev/null \

   303	  rmdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null || true

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# execute-agent.sh — agent-execution step for Loa Eval Sandbox trials
     4	#
     5	# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6). Fills the slot at the top of the
     6	# grading step in run-eval.sh: a task that declares `.agent.skill` runs the
     7	# headless Claude CLI inside the sandbox before its graders; every other task
     8	# takes the pre-existing path untouched.
     9	#
    10	# What it does, in order:
    11	#   1. Gate: no `.agent.skill` in the task YAML → exit 3, nothing written.
    12	#   2. Materialize the prompt surface from $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE into the sandbox:
    13	#        <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/        (SKILL.md + resources/)
    14	#        <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      (+ .claude/rules/)
    15	#        <ws>/CLAUDE.md                      → "@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    16	#        <ws>/.eval/skill-prompt.md          (SKILL.md body, frontmatter stripped)
    17	#      The prompt tree is the ONLY thing that differs between A/B arms, so it
    18	#      is recorded: prompt_tree_sha = `git rev-parse HEAD:.claude` of the tree,
    19	#      prompt_tree_commit, and whether .claude/ had uncommitted changes.
    20	#   3. Run:  claude -p "<task.prompt>" --output-format stream-json --verbose
    21	#              --model $EVAL_MODEL [--effort <e>] --restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Write
    22	#              --permission-mode acceptEdits --append-system-prompt-file <skill-prompt>
    23	#              --max-turns $EVAL_MAX_TURNS
    24	#      --restricted --tools names the SDD's fixed tool set EXACTLY: it removes the
    25	#      code-running tools, ignores the operator's user/project/local settings (their
    26	#      Bash(...) allow rules leaked into the sprint-237 A/B arms under --allowed-tools,
    27	#      which only adds rules) and confines Read/Grep/Glob/Write to the sandbox.
    28	#      Edit/MultiEdit are therefore unavailable; the transcript extractor below still
    29	#      records them defensively.
    30	#      cwd = sandbox; env-isolated (LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH / LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH and
    31	#      TMPDIR into the sandbox; GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/OPENAI_API_KEY/AWS_* unset;
    32	#      HOME and PATH stay so the CLI finds its own credentials and toolchain).
    33	#   4. Record <ws>/.eval/events.jsonl (raw stream), agent-output.json (the
    34	#      `result` event) and executor.json:
    35	#        {schema_version, skill, model_requested, model_id (the id the CLI
    36	#         echoed — the modelUsage entry with the most output tokens), effort,
    37	#         prompt_tree_sha, prompt_tree_commit, prompt_tree_dirty, exit_code,
    38	#         is_error, duration_ms, num_turns, total_cost_usd, usage{…},
    39	#         tool_writes:[{seq,tool,path}] in transcript order}
    40	#
    41	# Exit codes:
    42	#   0  agent ran (its own verdict is the graders' business)
    43	#   1  the CLI exited non-zero or timed out (executor.json still written)
    44	#   2  infrastructure error (CLI binary missing, prompt tree lacks the skill)
    45	#   3  task declares no agent (caller should not have called us)
    46	#
    47	# Env:
    48	#   EVAL_MODEL          model passed to --model            (default claude-sonnet-5)
    49	#   EVAL_EFFORT         override effort                    (default: task/skill)
    50	#   EVAL_PROMPT_TREE    repo whose .claude/ is materialized (default: this repo)
    51	#   EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN     CLI executable                     (default: claude)
    52	#   EVAL_MAX_TURNS      --max-turns                        (default 40)
    53	#
    54	# Control arms (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.1):
    55	#   LOA_EVAL_ARM          arm id (default baseline). Setting it at all is "arm
    56	#                         mode": the prompt tree's .loa.config.yaml is also
    57	#                         materialised so every arm sees the same config.
    58	#   LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES  JSON object {toggle: false, …}; when unset the arm is
    59	#                         resolved from LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, else from
    60	#                         evals/suites/<task dir name>.yaml (`ab.arms[]`)
    61	#   LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT  recorded as source_commit (default: the prompt
    62	#                         tree's HEAD)
    63	#   Toggles are applied to the SANDBOX COPY only, after every materialisation
    64	#   step and immediately before the executor starts; each is verified absent
    65	#   afterwards and a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never
    66	#   silently runs as its baseline):
    67	#     companion_voice: false         flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
    68	#                                    in <ws>/.loa.config.yaml (yq)
    69	#     karpathy_block: false          '## Karpathy Principles' section out of
    70	#                                    <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md; Karpathy rows
    71	#                                    out of <ws>/.claude/data/constraints.json if present
    72	#     rule_files: false              stash-safety.md, skill-invariants.md out of <ws>/.claude/rules/
    73	#     audit_delta_instruction: false the paragraph containing "look for what the
    74	#                                    review did not", else "Confirm the review's demotions
    75	#                                    independently", out of the sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md
    76	#   The appended skill prompt (.eval/skill-prompt.md) is derived from the
    77	#   toggled sandbox SKILL.md. executor.json records arm, arm_toggles,
    78	#   arm_evidence and source_commit.
    79	#
    80	# Tested by evals/tests/execute-agent.bats and evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats.
    81	# =============================================================================

   161	# The arm's toggles: explicit JSON, else the suite's ab.arms[] entry.
   162	resolve_toggles() {
   163	  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]]; then
   164	    jq -ce 'if type == "object" then . else error("not an object") end' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES" 2>/dev/null \
   165	      || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is not a JSON object" >&2; return 2; }

   167	  fi

   176	    [[ "$found" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || found=0

   189	
   190	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
   191	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
   192	_drop_md_section() {
   193	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
   194	  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
   195	  awk -v h="$heading" '
   196	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
   197	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
   198	    skip { n++; next }
   199	    { print }
   200	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
   201	  mv "$tmp" "$f"
   202	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
   206	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
   207	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
   208	_drop_paragraph() {
   209	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
   210	import re, sys
   211	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   212	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
   213	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
   214	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
   215	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
   216	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
   217	            removed = paras[i]
   218	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
   219	            del paras[i:i + 2]
   220	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
   221	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
   222	            sys.exit(0)
   223	sys.exit(1)
   224	PY
   225	}

   227	ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'

   230	apply_toggles() {
   231	  local key val
   232	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
   233	    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
   234	    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
   235	      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
   236	    fi
   237	    case "$key" in
   238	      companion_voice)
   239	        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
   240	        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
   241	        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
   242	          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
   243	        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
   244	          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
   245	        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
   246	        ;;
   247	      karpathy_block)

   250	        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"

   252	          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
   253	        fi
   254	        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
   255	        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
   256	          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
   257	        fi
   258	        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md"
   259	        ;;
   260	      rule_files)
   261	        local r gone=""
   262	        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do

   264	          [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
   265	        done
   266	        _evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
   267	        ;;
   268	      audit_delta_instruction)
   269	        local s="$WORKSPACE/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"

   272	          || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
   273	        _evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
   274	        ;;
   275	      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;
   276	    esac
   277	  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$ARM_TOGGLES")
   278	  return 0
   279	}

   377	     scope: (.scope // null)}' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc '.' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"

    11	
    12	# Git Stash Safety
    13	
    14	`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.
    15	
    16	**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.
    17	
    18	## The safe interface
    19	
    20	```bash
    21	source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
    22	stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
    23	```
    24	
    25	Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
    29	git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
    30	(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
    31	git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
    32	```
    33	
    34	## Judgment rules the fence cannot express
    35	
    36	- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
    37	- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

    11	
    12	# Git Stash Safety
    13	
    14	`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.
    15	
    16	**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.
    17	
    18	## The safe interface
    19	
    20	```bash
    21	source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
    22	stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
    23	```
    24	
    25	Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
    29	git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
    30	(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
    31	git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
    32	```
    33

    35	
    36	- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.

10	---
    11	
    12	# Skill Frontmatter Invariants
    13	
    14	SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.
    15	
    16	## The invariant
    17	
    18	When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.
    19	
    20	Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).
    21	
    22	## Agent type tool allowlists
    23	
    24	| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
    25	|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
    26	| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
    27	| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
    28	| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
    29	| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
    30	| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |
    31	
    32	Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.
    33	
    34	## Enforcement
    35	
    36	`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:
    37	
    38	> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …
    39	
    40	The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.
    41	
    42	## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)
    43	
    44	`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
    45	model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
    46	cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
    47	code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.
    48	
    49	| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
    50	|-------------|--------------------|-----|
    51	| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
    52	| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
    53	| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |
    54	
    55	**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
    56	`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
    57	`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
    58	the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
    59	orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
    60	`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
    61	skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
    62	a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
    63	path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
    64	which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.
    65	
    66	## Scope
    67	
    68	Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).
    69	
    70	## Origin
    71	
    72	- Defect: [#553](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/553) — `/architect` and `/sprint-plan` produced correct output but refused to write their target files. Three independent reproductions across two repos.
    73	- Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557) — Tier 1 cycle-083 framework boundary fixes.
    74	- Sprint: `sprint-bug-102` — test-first patch landing the invariant lint + the three frontmatter fixes.
    75	
    76	## Related rules
    77	
    78	- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` is framework-managed; SKILL.md edits require cycle-level authorization.
    79	- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — file-creation safety when authoring SKILL.md via heredoc.

--restricted --tools "Read,Grep,Glob,Write"
  --permission-mode acceptEdits
  --append-system-prompt-file "$eval_dir/skill-prompt.md"
  --max-turns "$MAX_TURNS"
)
[[ -n "$effort" ]] && argv+=(--effort "$effort")

events="$eval_dir/events.jsonl"
stderr_log="$eval_dir/agent-stderr.log"
start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
rc=0
(
  cd "$WORKSPACE" || exit 2
  export LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH="$eval_dir/model-invoke.jsonl"
  export LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH="$eval_dir/cost-ledger.jsonl"
  export EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL"
  # sprint-237 audit HIGH-001: the CLI keeps HOME (its own credentials live there)
  # and PATH (its toolchain); the operator's other credentials are not the agent
  # under test's business, and its temp files stay inside the sandbox.
  unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
  # cycle-129: an executor started from inside a Claude Code session inherits
  # that session's coupling (child-session flag, session id, messaging socket,
  # agent teams) and its subagent model (the sprint-255 driver session carried
  # CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=opus). Decouple the session and pin every
  # auxiliary model to the executor model. (A safeguard-refusal fallback to
  # another model is a separate CLI behaviour, recorded below as
  # refusal_fallbacks; no environment setting turns it off.)
  unset CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET \
    CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED
  export CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="$MODEL"
  mkdir -p "$eval_dir/tmp" && export TMPDIR="$eval_dir/tmp"
  exec timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15 "$TIMEOUT_S" "${argv[@]}"
) > "$events" 2> "$stderr_log" || rc=$?
end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
duration_ms=$(( end_ms - start_ms ))

# --- 4. record ---------------------------------------------------------------
# The last `result` event is the CLI's summary (absent on crash/timeout).
result_json="$(grep -E '^\{.*"type" *: *"result"' "$events" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
if [[ -z "$result_json" ]] || ! jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$result_json"; then
  result_json='{"type":"result","subtype":"missing","is_error":true}'
fi
printf '%s\n' "$result_json" > "$eval_dir/agent-output.json"

# Ordered tool writes from the transcript (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit).
tool_writes="$(jq -c '
  select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]? |
  select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Write" or .name=="Edit" or .name=="MultiEdit" or .name=="NotebookEdit")) |
  {tool:.name, path:(.input.file_path // .input.notebook_path // "")}
' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc 'to_entries | map({seq:(.key+1), tool:.value.tool, path:.value.path})' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"
[[ -n "$tool_writes" ]] || tool_writes='[]'

# cycle-129: a safeguard refusal makes the CLI retry the session on another
# model (system/model_refusal_fallback); the arm run must see it, because the
# output after it is not the requested executor's.
refusal_fallbacks="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="system" and .subtype=="model_refusal_fallback")
  | {from: (.original_model // null), to: (.fallback_model // null), category: (.api_refusal_category // null),
     scope: (.scope // null)}' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc '.' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"
[[ -n "$refusal_fallbacks" ]] || refusal_fallbacks='[]'

is_error="$(jq -r '.is_error // false' <<<"$result_json")"
[[ $rc -ne 0 ]] && is_error=true

jq -n \
  --arg skill "$skill" \
  --arg model_requested "$MODEL" \
  --arg effort "$effort" \
  --arg prompt_tree "$PROMPT_TREE" \
  --arg prompt_tree_sha "$prompt_tree_sha" \
  --arg prompt_tree_commit "$prompt_tree_commit" \
  --argjson prompt_tree_dirty "$prompt_tree_dirty" \
  --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" \
  --arg trial_id "$TRIAL_ID" \
  --argjson rc "$rc" \
  --argjson is_error "$is_error" \
  --argjson duration_ms "$duration_ms" \
  --argjson result "$result_json" \
  --argjson tool_writes "$tool_writes" \
  --arg arm "$ARM" \
  --argjson arm_toggles "$ARM_TOGGLES" \
  --argjson arm_evidence "$ARM_EVIDENCE" \
  --arg source_commit "${LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT:-$prompt_tree_commit}" \
  --argjson refusal_fallbacks "$refusal_fallbacks" \
  '
  def norm_usage(u): {
    input_tokens: (u.input_tokens // u.inputTokens // 0),
    output_tokens: (u.output_tokens // u.outputTokens // 0),
    cache_creation_input_tokens: (u.cache_creation_input_tokens // u.cacheCreationInputTokens // 0),
    cache_read_input_tokens: (u.cache_read_input_tokens // u.cacheReadInputTokens // 0)
  };
  ($result.modelUsage // {}) as $mu |
  # the model that produced the output: the modelUsage entry with the most
  # output tokens (a haiku helper call must not be mis-attributed — the
  # framework-review 2026-09-17 rec 5 class), else the requested id.
  (if ($mu | length) > 0
     then ($mu | to_entries | max_by(.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0) | .key)
     else $model_requested end) as $model_id |
  {
    schema_version: 1,
    skill: $skill,
    run_id: $run_id,
    trial_id: $trial_id,
    model_requested: $model_requested,
    model_id: $model_id,
    effort: $effort,
    prompt_tree: $prompt_tree,
    prompt_tree_sha: $prompt_tree_sha,
    prompt_tree_commit: $prompt_tree_commit,
    prompt_tree_dirty: $prompt_tree_dirty,
    exit_code: $rc,
    is_error: $is_error,
    duration_ms: $duration_ms,
    num_turns: ($result.num_turns // 0),
    total_cost_usd: ($result.total_cost_usd // 0),
    usage: norm_usage($result.usage // {}),
    models_used: ($mu | with_entries(.value = (.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0))),
    refusal_fallbacks: $refusal_fallbacks,
    tool_writes: $tool_writes,
    arm: $arm,
    arm_toggles: $arm_toggles,
    arm_evidence: $arm_evidence,
    source_commit: $source_commit
  }' > "$eval_dir/executor.json"

if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "execute-agent: CLI exited $rc (see $stderr_log)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys
    39	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    40	
    41	
    42	def load_yaml_subset(path):
    43	    """The suites are YAML (no stdlib parser); the harness already depends on yq v4."""
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    out = subprocess.run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    46	    return json.loads(out)
    47	
    48	
    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
    52	        return rows
    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    54	        for line in fh:
    55	            line = line.strip()
    56	            if line:
    57	                try:
    58	                    rows.append(json.loads(line))
    59	                except ValueError:
    60	                    continue
    61	    return rows
    62	
    63	
    64	def mean(xs):
    65	    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    66	    return sum(xs) / len(xs) if xs else None
    67	
    68	
    69	def fmt(x, nd=3):
    70	    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{x:.{nd}f}"
    71	
    72	
    73	def recall_details(row):
    74	    for g in row.get("graders") or []:
    75	        if g.get("name") == "recall-vs-defects.sh" and isinstance(g.get("details"), dict):
    76	            return g["details"]
    77	    return None
    78	
    79	
    80	def tokens(row):
    81	    u = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("usage") or {}
    82	    if not u:
    83	        return None
    84	    return sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
    85	               ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
    86	
    87	
    88	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
    89	    if not sorted_xs:
    90	        return None
    91	    k = max(0, min(len(sorted_xs) - 1, int(round(q * (len(sorted_xs) - 1)))))

    94	
    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))
   102	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0

   106	class Arm:
   107	    def __init__(self, arm_id):

   162	    def fixture_means(self):

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
     4	#
     5	# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
     6	# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
     7	# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
     8	# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    13	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    14	  REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/report.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
    16	  R="$T/arms"; S="$R/review-recall"; B="$S/b1"
    17	  mkdir -p "$B"
    18	  jq -n '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", batch:"b1", dry_run:false, source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457",
    19	          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
    20	    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
    21	  status_file complete
    22	}
    23	
    24	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    25	
    26	status_file() {  # status_file <state>
    27	  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
    28	                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
    29	}
    30	
    31	# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]
    32	row() {
    33	  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
    34	  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
    35	  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
    36	  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
    37	    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
    38	    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
    39	      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
    40	      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
    41	        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
    42	        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
    43	}
    44	
    45	full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
    46	  local fx t
    47	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
    48	}
    49	
    50	@test "AR-1 complete run: equal recall reads no recall loss, a large drop reads recall loss, the informational arm says so" {
    51	  full_arm baseline 1
    52	  full_arm no_rule_files 1
    53	  full_arm no_karpathy 0.3333 "L2,L3" 1
    54	  full_arm no_companion 1
    55	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --date 2026-10-14
    56	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    57	  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*'
    58	  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
    59	  grep -E '^\| `no_companion` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q 'informational: yield only'
    60	  grep -E '^\| `baseline` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '(reference)'
    61	  # the interval of the drop and the missed labels are printed
    62	  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\[0.667, 0.667\]'
    63	  grep -q 'no_karpathy`: pr-01:L2 (3/3)' "$T/r.md"
    64	  grep -q '^# Control-arm report — 2026-10-14' "$T/r.md"
    65	  ! grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
    66	}
    67	
    68	@test "AR-2 a refuted-share rise beyond the threshold is a recall loss even with equal recall" {
    69	  full_arm baseline 1 "" 0
    70	  full_arm no_rule_files 1 "" 3
    71	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
    72	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    73	  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
    74	  grep -q 'refuted share 0.750 > baseline 0.000' "$T/r.md"
    75	}
    76	
    77	@test "AR-3 a missing trial or fixture is inconclusive; model or source skew is inconclusive" {
    78	  full_arm baseline 1
    79	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_rule_files "$fx" "$t" 1 ""; done; done
    80	  row no_rule_files pr-03 1 1 ""
    81	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_karpathy "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-opus-5-5; done; done
    82	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_companion "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-fable-5-1 ffd25258; done; done
    83	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
    84	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    85	  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
    86	  grep -q 'coverage: pr-03 1/3' "$T/r.md"
    87	  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
    88	  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
    89	  grep -q 'source skew' "$T/r.md"
    90	}
    91	
    92	@test "AR-4 a rule violation within the baseline's own trial-to-trial spread names no change (inconclusive)" {
    93	  # baseline trial means 1.0, 0.6, 1.0 (spread 0.4); the arm sits 0.2 lower on every fixture
    94	  local fx
    95	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row baseline "$fx" 1 1 ""; row baseline "$fx" 2 0.6 ""; row baseline "$fx" 3 1 ""; done
    96	  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row no_rule_files "$fx" 1 0.8 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 2 0.4 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 3 0.8 ""; done
    97	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
    98	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    99	  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
   100	  grep -q 'no change can be named' "$T/r.md"
   101	}
   102	
   103	@test "AR-5 STATUS.json not complete: refused (exit 1); --partial writes, says so, and every verdict is inconclusive" {
   104	  full_arm baseline 1
   105	  full_arm no_rule_files 1
   106	  status_file running
   107	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
   108	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   109	  grep -q "not 'complete'" <<<"$output"
   110	  [ ! -e "$T/r.md" ]
   111	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --partial
   112	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   113	  grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
   114	  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
   115	  ! grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*' "$T/r.md"
   116	}
   117	
   118	@test "AR-7 a safeguard-refusal fallback to another model is skew: the arm is inconclusive and the fallback is named" {
   119	  full_arm baseline 1
   120	  full_arm no_rule_files 1
   121	  # one no_rule_files trial moved to Opus on a refusal (models_used + refusal_fallbacks, as execute-agent records them)
   122	  jq -c 'if .trial == 1 and .fixture == "pr-01" then .executor.models_used = {"claude-fable-5-1": 10, "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 90}
   123	         | .executor.refusal_fallbacks = [{"from":"claude-fable-5-1","to":"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5","category":"cyber"}] else . end' \
   124	    "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl" > "$B/x" && mv "$B/x" "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl"
   125	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
   126	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   127	  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
   128	  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
   129	  grep -q '1/9 trial(s) fell back to another model on a safeguard refusal' "$T/r.md"
   130	}
   131	
   132	@test "AR-6 the default output path is evals/results/arms-report-<date>.md under the results root's repo; bad args exit 2" {
   133	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite nope --results-dir "$R"
   134	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   135	  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$T/missing" --out "$T/r.md"

# --- PHASE: LOAD_SUITE ---
load_tasks() {
  TASK_FILES=()

  if [[ -n "$TASK_ID" ]]; then
    # Single task mode
    local task_file
    task_file="$(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name "${TASK_ID}.yaml" -o -name "${TASK_ID}.yml" | head -1)"
    if [[ -z "$task_file" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Task not found: $TASK_ID" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    TASK_FILES=("$task_file")
    [[ -z "$SUITE" ]] && SUITE="single"
    log "[LOAD] Loaded single task: $TASK_ID"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -n "$SKILL" ]]; then
    # Skill filter mode
    while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
      local task_skill
      task_skill="$(yq -r '.skill // ""' "$task_file")"
      if [[ "$task_skill" == "$SKILL" ]]; then
        TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
      fi
    done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | tr '\n' '\0')
    [[ -z "$SUITE" ]] && SUITE="skill-$SKILL"
    log "[LOAD] Found ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks for skill: $SKILL"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -n "$SUITE" ]]; then
    local suite_file="$SUITES_DIR/${SUITE}.yaml"
    if [[ ! -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Suite not found: $suite_file" >&2
      exit 3
    fi

    # Read include patterns from suite
    local include_count
    include_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.include | length // 0' "$suite_file")"

    for i in $(seq 0 $((include_count - 1))); do
      local pattern
      pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.include[$i]" "$suite_file")"

      # Resolve glob pattern relative to evals/
      # Use bash globbing with globstar for ** patterns
      local had_globstar=false
      shopt -q globstar 2>/dev/null && had_globstar=true
      shopt -s globstar 2>/dev/null || true

      local glob_expanded=false
      for task_file in $EVALS_DIR/$pattern; do
        if [[ -f "$task_file" ]]; then
          TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          glob_expanded=true
        fi
      done

      # Restore globstar
      if [[ "$had_globstar" == "false" ]]; then
        shopt -u globstar 2>/dev/null || true
      fi

      # Fallback: if glob didn't match, try find in the directory
      if [[ "$glob_expanded" == "false" ]]; then
        # Extract directory portion from pattern
        local pattern_dir="${pattern%/*}"
        if [[ -d "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
            TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          done < <(find "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
      fi
    done

    # Apply exclude patterns
    local exclude_count
    exclude_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.exclude | length // 0' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")"
    if [[ "$exclude_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
      local filtered_tasks=()
      for task_file in "${TASK_FILES[@]}"; do
        local excluded=false
        for j in $(seq 0 $((exclude_count - 1))); do
          local exclude_pattern
          exclude_pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.exclude[$j]" "$suite_file")"
          if [[ "$(basename "$task_file")" == $exclude_pattern ]]; then
            excluded=true
            break
          fi
        done
        [[ "$excluded" == "false" ]] && filtered_tasks+=("$task_file")
      done
      TASK_FILES=("${filtered_tasks[@]}")
    fi

    # Read suite defaults
    SUITE_TRIALS="$(yq -r '.defaults.trials // 1' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_trial // 120' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_GRADER="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_grader // 30' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_STRATEGY="$(yq -r '.defaults.composite_strategy // "all_must_pass"' "$suite_file")"

    log "[LOAD] Suite '$SUITE': ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks, ${SUITE_TRIALS} trial(s)"
    return
  fi

  # Default: run all tasks
  while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
    TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
  done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | sort | tr '\n' '\0')
  SUITE="all"
  log "[LOAD] Loaded ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks (all)"
}

# Suite defaults
SUITE_TRIALS=1
SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL=120

ab:
  floor_commit: "da3bd07f3db2fc1bd09a6761a9b96b688fa2a09e"
  corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS

  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
  #                can never license removing the control
  arms:
    - id: baseline
      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
      toggles: {}
    - id: no_companion
      description: >-
        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
      informational: true
      toggles:
        companion_voice: false
    - id: no_karpathy
      description: >-
        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
      toggles:
        karpathy_block: false
    - id: no_rule_files
      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
      toggles:
        rule_files: false

  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
  threshold:
    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
    trials_required: 3
    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
    coverage_required: full
    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with
    # replacement `iterations` times, report the `level` two-sided interval
    bootstrap:
      method: percentile
      level: 0.90
      resample: fixtures
      iterations: 2000

ci:
  gate_type: advisory
  min_trials: 3
  regression_threshold: 0.10

execution_order: parallel
concurrency: 2

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD §1.6, D-9.2)
     5	# The floor does not move: every floor_files entry of .claude/data/floor.yaml
     6	# and the fence-corpus rows named under floor_corpus are byte-identical to
     7	# origin/main; the register disables nothing, so the .claude/settings.json hook
     8	# registrations and the fence's pattern-id call-site list are identical too.
     9	# Skipped, with a message, when origin/main is not reachable (a shallow CI
    10	# checkout); the floor.yaml sha256 pin in guard-origins.bats still runs there.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {
    14	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    15	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    16	  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    17	  if ! git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q 'origin/main^{commit}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    18	    skip "origin/main is not reachable from this checkout (shallow clone?): the floor snapshot needs it — run 'git fetch origin main'"
    19	  fi
    20	  BASE="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse 'origin/main^{commit}')"
    21	}
    22	
    23	base_show() { git -C "$ROOT" show "$BASE:$1"; }
    24	
    25	@test "FS-1 every floor_files entry is byte-identical to origin/main" {
    26	  n=0
    27	  while IFS= read -r f; do
    28	    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
    29	    n=$((n + 1))
    30	    git -C "$ROOT" cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" || { echo "$f is not on origin/main" >&2; false; }
    31	    base_show "$f" | cmp -s - "$ROOT/$f" || { echo "floor file $f differs from origin/main" >&2; false; }
    32	  done < <(yq -r '.floor_files[]' "$FLOOR")
    33	  [ "$n" -ge 4 ]
    34	}
    35	
    36	@test "FS-2 the fence-corpus rows named in floor_corpus (FR-1.2b, FR-SZ*) are identical to origin/main" {
    37	  corpus="$(yq -r '.floor_corpus.file' "$FLOOR")"
    38	  rules="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.floor_corpus.rules' "$FLOOR")"
    39	  sel='def m($r): $r | any(.[]; . as $p | if ($p | endswith("*")) then ($in.rule // "" | startswith($p | rtrimstr("*"))) else ($in.rule // "") == $p end);
    40	       . as $in | select(m($rules))'
    41	  diff <(base_show "$corpus" | jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel") <(jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel" "$ROOT/$corpus")
    42	}
    43	
    44	@test "FS-3 the register disables nothing: settings.json hook registrations are identical to origin/main" {
    45	  diff <(base_show .claude/settings.json | jq -c '.hooks') <(jq -c '.hooks' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")
    46	}
    47	
    48	@test "FS-4 the fence's pattern-id call-site list (in order) is identical to origin/main" {
    49	  ids() { grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"'; }

# run-eval.sh:379 slot. It is gated on a task's `.agent.skill`; it
# materializes the prompt surface (skill body without frontmatter, CLAUDE.md
# → CLAUDE.loa.md, rules) from $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE into the sandbox, runs the
# headless CLI with a fixed tool set, and records executor.json (model id the
# CLI echoed, usage, prompt_tree_sha, ordered tool writes). The CLI is
# replaced by evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh here.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
  STUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ea.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"
  mkdir -p "$WS"
  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$STUB"
  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5"
  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$REPO_ROOT"
  export STUB_ARGV_FILE="$T/argv"
  export STUB_ENV_FILE="$T/env"
  unset EVAL_EFFORT
  # A task that declares an agent (the executor's gate).
  cat > "$T/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: ea-task
schema_version: 1
skill: reviewing-code
category: skill-quality
fixture: hello-world-ts
description: "executor test task"
prompt: "Read REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md and carry it out."
agent:
  skill: reviewing-code
  artifacts: [review.md]
graders:
  - type: code

    args: ["review.md"]
YAML
  # The same task without an agent block.

# compare.sh freshness rule (evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats):
# a baseline must be captured at or after floor_commit (the Sprint-2 landing
# commit) on a prompt tree different from the one under comparison, with the
# corpus frozen.
ab:
  floor_commit: "da3bd07f3db2fc1bd09a6761a9b96b688fa2a09e"
  corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS

  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
  #                can never license removing the control
  arms:
    - id: baseline
      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
      toggles: {}
    - id: no_companion
      description: >-
        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
      informational: true
      toggles:
        companion_voice: false
    - id: no_karpathy
      description: >-
        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
      toggles:
        karpathy_block: false
    - id: no_rule_files
      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
      toggles:
        rule_files: false

  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
  threshold:
    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
    trials_required: 3
    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
    coverage_required: full
    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with

    bootstrap:

fi

  cp -a "$PROMPT_TREE/.claude/rules/." "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/"
fi
