# --- 2b. control arm (cycle-129 FR-2) -----------------------------------------
ARM_MODE=false
[[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" ]] && ARM_MODE=true
ARM="${LOA_EVAL_ARM:-baseline}"
[[ "$ARM" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { echo "ERROR: invalid LOA_EVAL_ARM '$ARM'" >&2; exit 2; }
if [[ "$ARM_MODE" == "true" && -f "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
  cp "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml" "$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
fi

# The arm's toggles: explicit JSON, else the suite's ab.arms[] entry.
resolve_toggles() {
  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]]; then
    jq -ce 'if type == "object" then . else error("not an object") end' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES" 2>/dev/null \
      || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is not a JSON object" >&2; return 2; }
    return 0
  fi
  local suite_file="${LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE:-}"
  if [[ -z "$suite_file" ]]; then
    local tdir; tdir="$(basename "$(dirname "$TASK_YAML")")"
    [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml" ]] && suite_file="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml"
  fi
  local t="" found=0
  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
    found="$(ARM="$ARM" yq '[.ab.arms[]? | select(.id == strenv(ARM))] | length' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [[ "$found" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || found=0
    if [[ "$found" -gt 0 ]]; then
      t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]; then
    [[ "$ARM" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
    echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (ab.arms[])" >&2
    return 2
  fi
  printf '%s' "$t"
}
ARM_TOGGLES="$(resolve_toggles)" || exit 2

# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
_drop_md_section() {
  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
  awk -v h="$heading" '
    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
    skip { n++; next }
    { print }
    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"

name: review-recall
description: "cycle-124 FR-9 A/B suite: review-recall (arm A = Sprint-2 tip prompts, arm B = audited prompts; same executor model, fixed effort)"
version: 1

tasks:
  include:
    - "tasks/review-recall/**/*.yaml"
  exclude: []

defaults:
  trials: 3
  timeout:
    per_trial: 1500
    per_grader: 180
  composite_strategy: all_must_pass

# compare.sh freshness rule (evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats):
# a baseline must be captured at or after floor_commit (the Sprint-2 landing
# commit) on a prompt tree different from the one under comparison, with the
# corpus frozen.
ab:
  floor_commit: "da3bd07f3db2fc1bd09a6761a9b96b688fa2a09e"
  corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS

  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
  #                can never license removing the control
  arms:
    - id: baseline
      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
      toggles: {}
    - id: no_companion
      description: >-
        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
      informational: true
      toggles:
        companion_voice: false
    - id: no_karpathy
      description: >-
        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
      toggles:
        karpathy_block: false
    - id: no_rule_files
      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
      toggles:
        rule_files: false

  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
  threshold:
    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
    trials_required: 3
    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
    coverage_required: full
    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with
    # replacement `iterations` times, report the `level` two-sided interval
    bootstrap:
      method: percentile
      level: 0.90

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# recall-vs-defects.sh — deterministic planted-defect recall grader
#
# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9). Args: $1=workspace, $2=fixture id (pr-NN),
# $3=review file (default review.md). Reads the HIDDEN manifest
# evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/<id>.json (never copied into the
# sandbox) and the agent's review.
#
# Rule (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol, no fuzzy adjudication): a defect is DETECTED
# when the review contains a `path:line` (or `path:line-line`) citation whose
# path ends with the defect's file (repo-relative, `head/`-prefixed, or the
# bare basename) and whose line, or line range, falls within ±3 of the
# manifest anchor — `anchor_line`, or any line in `anchors[]` for a defect
# with more than one site.
#
# Parser (1.1.0, bd-ewrc): a leading `(` is not part of the path; comma
# continuations (`path:776,807`, `path:10, 118-121`) and a later bare `:N` or
# `head:N` / `base:N` bind to the most recent cited path. A `:N` glued to a
# word or a number (`note:40`, `10:40`), or with no cited path before it,
# credits nothing.
#
# Parser 1.1.1 (sprint-250 review run 1, n40-n42): the LOA-VERDICT trailer is
# removed before citations are parsed, and a bare `:N` after a quote, bracket,
# brace or `*` (JSON such as `"high":3`) credits nothing; a backtick- or
# bold-wrapped path (`` `b.sh`:40 ``, `**b.sh**:40`) binds its own line; a comma
# continuation or range stays on its line, and a continuation must end at a
# number boundary (no dates);
# a path containing `//` (a URL) is not a citation.
# Run 2 (#11/#13-#15): a match inside any URL token (`scheme://...`) is not a
# citation; a range dash is unspaced and every number (first, continuation,
# bare) ends at a boundary (no further `-N` / `–N`: no dates); the
# quote/bracket guard applies only to the fully bare `:N` (plus a closing
# backtick), so `"head:40"` binds as in 1.1.0; one trailer pattern strips and
# reads the LOA-VERDICT comment and never crosses another comment's bounds.
# Parser 1.1.2 (the run 2 changes above, plus sprint-250 review run 3): the
# URL look-back takes the text after the last whitespace — one linear split —
# so a citation that opens a line never inherits the previous line's URL.
# The parser runs as `python3 -I -` (audit dissent run 1, n32): a module planted
# in the invoker's cwd (a forging json.py) is never imported (RG-27).
#
# Grader 1.2.0 (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3): adds the refuted-share figure;
# the recall rule and the pass/score contract are unchanged. A FINDING is one
# distinct cited (path, line-range); it is MATCHED when it overlaps (±3) a
# defect site or a manifest `fix_regions[]` entry ({file, start, end}: the
# head-side lines a record fixture's fix commit touched). details gain
# findings_cited, findings_refuted and refuted_share (refuted / cited; null
# when nothing is cited).
#
# Clean fixtures (0 planted defects) measure FALSE POSITIVES: the LOA-VERDICT
# trailer's critical+high counts; without a trailer, every file:line citation
# counts as one.
#
# Output: {"pass", "score", "details":{recall, planted, detected[], missed[],
#          false_positives, severity_counts, model, effort, tokens}, "grader_version"}
#   pass  = every planted defect detected (defect fixture) / zero false
#           positives (clean fixture); score = recall*100 or 100/0.
# Exit: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error (missing manifest / bad args)
#
# Tested by evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

workspace="${1:-}"
fixture="${2:-}"
review_name="${3:-review.md}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
MANIFEST_DIR="${EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../fixtures/review-prs/manifests}"

  exit 1
fi

python3 -I - "$manifest" "$review" "$executor" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
manifest_path, review_path, executor_path = sys.argv[1:4]
man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue
    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
        return True
    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

detected, missed = [], []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    sites = d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]
    hit = any(path_matches(p, d["file"]) and not (b < s - 3 or a > s + 3)
              for p, a, b in cites for s in sites)
    (detected if hit else missed).append(d["id"])

planted = len(man.get("defects", []))
recall = round(len(detected) / planted, 4) if planted else None

# refuted share (1.2.0): distinct cited findings that touch no defect site and
# no fix region. Regions are (file, lo, hi) on head/ line numbers, widened ±3.
regions = []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]):
        regions.append((d["file"], s - 3, s + 3))
for fr in man.get("fix_regions", []) or []:
    try:
        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        continue
findings = sorted(set(cites))
refuted = [c for c in findings
           if not any(path_matches(c[0], f) and not (c[2] < lo or c[1] > hi) for f, lo, hi in regions)]
refuted_share = round(len(refuted) / len(findings), 4) if findings else None

# trailer → severity counts (false positives on clean fixtures)
sev = None
tm = TRAILER.search(text)
if tm:
    try:
        sev = json.loads(tm.group(1)).get("counts")
    except Exception:
        sev = None
if isinstance(sev, dict):
    fp = int(sev.get("critical", 0) or 0) + int(sev.get("high", 0) or 0)
else:
    fp = len({(p, a, b) for p, a, b in cites})
false_positives = fp if planted == 0 else 0

model = effort = None
tokens = None
try:
    ex = json.load(open(executor_path))
    model, effort = ex.get("model_id"), ex.get("effort")
    u = ex.get("usage") or {}
    # every token the call consumed: uncached input, cache writes, cache
    # reads and output — the prompt surface is mostly CACHED input, so
    # input_tokens alone (30 on a real run) would hide the very thing the
    # prompt diet changes
    tokens = sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
                 ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
except Exception:
    pass

if planted:
    ok = len(missed) == 0
    score = int(round(recall * 100))
else:
    ok = false_positives == 0
    score = 100 if ok else 0

out = {
    "pass": ok,
    "score": score,
    "details": {
        "recall": recall, "planted": planted, "detected": detected, "missed": missed,
        "false_positives": false_positives, "severity_counts": sev,
        "citations": len(cites), "model": model, "effort": effort, "tokens": tokens,
        "findings_cited": len(findings), "findings_refuted": len(refuted),
        "refuted_share": refuted_share,
    },
    "grader_version": "1.2.0",
}
print(json.dumps(out))
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.1)
     4	#
     5	# execute-agent.sh applies a control arm's toggles to the sandbox copy only.
     6	# Every assertion here reads the sandbox as the EXECUTOR saw it: the CLI stub
     7	# snapshots CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and the appended system
     8	# prompt at the moment it starts (STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR), after every
     9	# materialisation step. The arm ids and toggles come from the real suite
    10	# files; the prompt tree is a synthetic fixture so later prose edits to the
    11	# live kernel cannot change what this test proves.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	setup() {
    15	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    16	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    17	  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
    18	  REVIEW_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml"
    19	  AUDIT_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/audit-recall.yaml"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/at.XXXXXX")"
    21	  WS="$T/ws"; SNAP="$T/snap"
    22	  mkdir -p "$WS"
    23	  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
    24	  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
    25	  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
    26	  export STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR="$SNAP"
    27	  unset LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT EVAL_EFFORT
    28	
    29	  # --- synthetic prompt tree (the shape of 864069f2) ---
    30	  PT="$T/tree"
    31	  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/loa" "$PT/.claude/rules" "$PT/.claude/data" \
    32	    "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code" "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security"
    33	  printf '%s\n' "# Loa Framework Instructions" "" "## Three-Zone Model" "" "zones" "" \
    34	    "## Karpathy Principles" "" "Every code-touching turn." "" "1. **Think before coding** — state assumptions." "" \
    35	    "## Process Compliance" "" "rules" > "$PT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    36	  echo "# Git Stash Safety" > "$PT/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
    37	  echo "# Skill Frontmatter Invariants" > "$PT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
    38	  printf '%s\n' "---" "paths:" '  - "grimoires/**"' "---" "# zone state" > "$PT/.claude/rules/zone-state.md"
    39	  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" "Review the diff." > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
    40	  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: auditing-security" "---" "# Audit" "" "### Coverage" "" \
    41	    "Report every finding you actually observe." "" \
    42	    "Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under" \
    43	    "\`excluded\`, either confirm it or tally it as a finding of your own." "" \
    44	    "## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally" "" "Count every finding." > "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
    45	  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" "  security_audit:" "    enabled: true" > "$PT/.loa.config.yaml"
    46	  ( cd "$PT" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m tree )
    47	  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$PT"
    48	
    49	  for s in reviewing-code auditing-security; do
    50	    cat > "$T/task-$s.yaml" <<YAML
    51	id: at-$s
    52	schema_version: 1
    53	skill: $s
    54	category: skill-quality
    55	fixture: hello-world-ts
    56	description: "arm toggle task"
    57	prompt: "Read the instructions and carry them out."
    58	agent:
    59	  skill: $s
    60	  artifacts: [review.md]
    61	graders:
    62	  - type: code
    63	    script: file-exists.sh
    64	    args: ["review.md"]
    65	YAML
    66	  done
    67	}
    68	
    69	teardown() {
    70	  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
    71	  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
    72	}
    73	
    74	run_arm() {  # run_arm <arm> <suite-file> <skill>
    75	  LOA_EVAL_ARM="$1" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$2" run "$EXEC" --task-yaml "$T/task-$3.yaml" --workspace "$WS"
    76	}
    77	
    78	@test "AT-1 both suites declare the canonical arm ids and the pre-registered threshold block" {
    79	  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$REVIEW_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files" ]
    80	  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$AUDIT_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_audit_delta" ]
    81	  [ "$(yq -r '.ab.arms[] | select(.id=="no_companion") | .informational' "$REVIEW_SUITE")" = "true" ]
    82	  yq -r '.ab.arms[] | select(.id=="no_karpathy") | .description' "$REVIEW_SUITE" | grep -q 'kernel block only'
    83	  for s in "$REVIEW_SUITE" "$AUDIT_SUITE"; do
    84	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.trials_required' "$s")" = "3" ]
    85	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.coverage_required' "$s")" = "full" ]
    86	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.mean_recall_max_drop' "$s")" = "0.10" ]
    87	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.min_trial_recall_max_drop' "$s")" = "0.15" ]
    88	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.refuted_share_max_rise' "$s")" = "0.10" ]
    89	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.bootstrap | [.method, .level, .resample, .iterations] | join(",")' "$s")" = "percentile,0.90,fixtures,2000" ]
    90	    # the existing freshness keys are untouched
    91	    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.corpus_manifest' "$s")" = "evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS" ]
    92	  done
    93	}

I found five defects. Four are in `seed-corpus.bats` and its fixture setup, and two are in `seed-corpus-from-record.sh`; one item covers both files.

All 6 bats tests pass on a copy in `~/h2`. Two things had to change for them to run there. First, the snapshot has the scripts as 644 and `/tmp` is noexec, so I ran from my home dir with `chmod +x`. Second, `evals/graders/no-secrets.sh` isn't in the snapshot, so I used a stub that greps for the AWS-key and GitHub-token patterns.

1. **`head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69, 90, 91, 143`** — These negated assertions are no-ops. Bats does not fail a test on a `! cmd` line unless it is the test's last line. I confirmed this here: `! true` in the middle of a test, and the test still passed. So these claims are never checked:
   - line 69: "the previous-round section is never read"
   - line 90: SC-2's headline claim "nothing written carries the key"
   - line 91: "no c.sh label"
   - line 143: "no stale corpus row"

   The usual fix is `run ! …` or `! cmd || false`.

2. **`head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:159-161`** (with `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295, 730, 743-745`) — The SC-6 case "a non-record fixture is refused" never reaches the refusal.
   - The test's `pr-01` has no `fixture.yaml`, so the check at line 295 (`os.path.isfile(fy) and "\nsprint:" not in …`) does not fire.
   - The seed carries on and runs `shutil.rmtree(fdir)` on `pr-01`, which deletes the instruction templates.
   - It then crashes at line 745 with `FileNotFoundError: …/corpus/pr-01/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md`, because it copies the templates from the directory it just deleted.
   - The test only checks exit 1 and that `fixture.yaml` is absent, so it passes on that traceback. I reproduced this: afterwards `pr-01` holds only `PR.md`, `base/`, `head/` and `head.diff`.
   - In the script itself, any `pr-NN` dir without a `fixture.yaml` is wiped rather than refused.

3. **`head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:37-39` vs `418-460`** — The header says bridgebuilder labels come from "bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only". But `parse_findings(name, text)` never uses `name`.
   - Every `- **SEV**` bullet and `### [SEV]` heading in a bridgebuilder file becomes a finding, not just the Fixed table.
   - A `## Fixed` table inside an engineer-feedback or auditor file is also parsed into findings. That contradicts the header's own rule.

4. **`head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312`** — Detecting renamed binary files breaks on git's brace form. For a binary renamed inside a directory, `git diff --numstat -M` prints `d/{a.png => b.png}` (I checked). `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` turns that into `b.png`, not `d/b.png`; for `x/{a => b}/f.png` it gives `b}/f.png`.
   - The file is then missing from `binary`, so it passes the filter at line 321.
   - It gets copied into `base/` and `head/` through `redact()`, which decodes with `errors="replace"` and re-encodes, so the copies are corrupted.
   - This breaks the "without binaries" scope promise at line 33.

5. **`head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:12, 257-258`** (minor) — The `--approve` usage and error text require `--by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"`. The check `^[A-Za-z0-9 ._@-]{3,80}$` never looks for a date, so `--by "abc"` approves the fixture. That approval is what `run-arms.sh` (line 115) trusts.

Everything else in scope looked clean:
- **Task files:** the sixteen `tasks/{review,audit}-recall/*-pr-1[1-8].yaml` files are consistent with each other, with the generator template (lines 780-791), with the suites' `tasks/<suite>/**/*.yaml` globs, and with the README's pr-11…pr-18 = sprints 247–254. I couldn't check the label counts in the descriptions, because the manifests aren't in the snapshot.
- **`build-review-corpus.sh`:** the change skips `#` comment lines and `record` rows correctly, and still freezes the whole corpus.

   - Every `- **SEV**` bullet and `### [SEV]` heading in a bridgebuilder file becomes a finding, not just the Fixed table.
   - A `## Fixed` table inside an engineer-feedback or auditor file is also parsed into findings. That contradicts the header's own rule.

4. **`head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312`** — Detecting renamed binary files breaks on git's brace form. For a binary renamed inside a directory, `git diff --numstat -M` prints `d/{a.png => b.png}` (I checked). `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` turns that into `b.png`, not `d/b.png`; for `x/{a => b}/f.png` it gives `b}/f.png`.
   - The file is then missing from `binary`, so it passes the filter at line 321.
   - It gets copied into `base/` and `head/` through `redact()`, which decodes with `errors="replace"` and re-encodes, so the copies are corrupted.
   - This breaks the "without binaries" scope promise at line 33.

5. **`head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:12, 257-258`** (minor) — The `--approve` usage and error text require `--by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"`. The check `^[A-Za-z0-9 ._@-]{3,80}$` never looks for a date, so `--by "abc"` approves the fixture. That approval is what `run-arms.sh` (line 115) trusts.

Everything else in scope looked clean:
- **Task files:** the sixteen `tasks/{review,audit}-recall/*-pr-1[1-8].yaml` files are consistent with each other, with the generator template (lines 780-791), with the suites' `tasks/<suite>/**/*.yaml` globs, and with the README's pr-11…pr-18 = sprints 247–254. I found five defects in the reviewed files. I confirmed the first three by running copies of `execute-agent.sh` and the stub under `$HOME/rvtest`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec. Nothing in `/workspace/pr` was changed.

**Defects**

- `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:260-266` — `rule_files` succeeds when neither rule file exists. It records `"removed: none present"`, exits 0, and the arm runs exactly as baseline. The header (lines 63-66) promises the opposite: "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)". Reproduced with `LOA_EVAL_ARM=no_rule_files` on a prompt tree with no `.claude/rules/`: rc=0, evidence `{"rule_files":"removed: none present"}`. This hits any pinned source commit from before those rule files existed.

- `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:271-273` — `audit_delta_instruction` never re-checks the file after removing the paragraph, although the header (line 64) says "each is verified absent afterwards". `_drop_paragraph` removes only the first paragraph that matches. If the needle appears in more than one paragraph, the delta instruction stays in the prompt and the run still exits 0. Reproduced: with the needle in two paragraphs, the generated `skill-prompt.md` still contained "Look for what the review did not catch". The same gap exists at `:243`, where `companion_voice` checks only `code_review.companion_voice` and not `security_audit`.

- `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:153-158, 163-166, 398` — if `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES` is set without `LOA_EVAL_ARM`, the toggles are applied but the run is recorded as `arm: "baseline"`. `run-eval.sh` copies `executor.arm` into the result rows, so a modified run is labelled baseline there too. That run also skips copying `.loa.config.yaml`, so `companion_voice` creates a config holding only that one key. Reproduced: `{"arm":"baseline","arm_toggles":{"karpathy_block":false,...}}`. The check at `:234` also accepts the string `"false"`, not just boolean false.

- `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:195-198` — `_drop_md_section` ignores code fences. A `## ` line inside a fenced block in the Karpathy section ends the skip early. What's left starts mid-block (`## not a heading`, then an unmatched closing fence), and the rest of the section survives. The check at `:251` still passes. Reproduced on a sample `CLAUDE.loa.md`.

- `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:343-349` — the comment says "pin every auxiliary model to the executor model", but the code only exports `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`. Nothing pins the small/fast helper model. The same file (`:411-413`) admits that haiku helper calls happen.

**Lower-severity issues**

- `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:375-377` — `refusal_fallbacks` repeats the `jq … | jq -sc . || echo '[]'` pattern. If `events.jsonl` ends in a truncated line (a timeout mid-write), `pipefail` makes the value two JSON texts (`[...]\n[]`). `--argjson` then fails, leaving an empty `executor.json` and exit 2 instead of 1. Reproduced. The same bug already exists for `tool_writes` at `:365-369`, so this change adds a second copy rather than introducing it.

- `head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-kind-01.yml:25` — the grader regex `[*][*]MEDIUM[*][*].*[Mm]echanical` doesn't check the citation (`fixture.yaml` expects `head/.claude/skills/run-status/SKILL.md:13-17`). It also matches a demoted `**MEDIUM** (speculative…)` entry under `## Observations`, and a line like "**MEDIUM** … not mechanical". So it can't confirm the finding the task describes.

I found no defects in `claude-stub.sh`, the EA-11/EA-12 tests in `execute-agent.bats`, or the `kind-01` fixture files. The fixture's lines 13-17 match the expected citation, and the claim that the `.yml` extension keeps the task out of the suite holds.

content.text:
I found 8 defects in this PR. The first three affect verdicts and exit codes; the rest are test gaps and harness behaviour. I confirmed #1 and #2 by running `arms-report.py` on synthetic results, and the claim behind #4 with a small bats file (bats 1.13). The rest come from reading the code.

**Verdict and statistics bugs**

1. `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:302` — **An arm with better recall can be labelled "recall loss".** The "too small to name" exception tests `abs(drop) <= base_spread`. The docstring (lines 19–23) says the exception applies when the drop "does not exceed the baseline's own trial-to-trial spread". Using `abs()` sends a large *negative* drop (the arm recalls more than baseline) to `recall loss` whenever the confidence interval's upper bound or the min-trial rule trips.
   - Test case: baseline recall per fixture 1/0.05/0.05, arm 0/0.95/0.95. Output: arm mean 0.633 vs baseline 0.367, drop −0.267, CI [−0.900, 0.367], verdict **recall loss**.
   - Line 324 has the same `abs()` and prints "change named" for an improvement.

2. `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:240-241` — **Coverage is never enforced on clean fixtures.** `coverage_gaps` skips any fixture with `planted == 0`. The docstring (lines 17–18) says "a planned fixture lacks trials_required completed trials … → inconclusive", and the suite YAML says "every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials". The clean fixtures still feed the refuted-share rule.
   - Test case: arm has the clean fixture pr-02 at 1/3 trials, defect fixture pr-01 at 3/3. Verdict: **no recall loss** with no coverage note.

3. `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:181,201,45` together with `head/evals/harness/report.sh:56` — **Errors exit 1, which is documented as "refused".** The docstring (line 30) and `report.sh` usage say 1 = refused, 2 = error. But an unreadable STATUS.json or MANIFEST.json, or a failing `yq` (`check=True`), raises an uncaught exception and Python exits 1. Confirmed: a malformed STATUS.json gives a `JSONDecodeError` traceback and rc=1, indistinguishable from "not complete".

**Tests that cannot catch what they claim**

4. `head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132,133,152,153,166` — **The key negative checks can never fail.** Each is a `! grep -q …` that is not the last command in its test, and bash `set -e` ignores `!`-negated commands. Verified: a test containing `! true; true` passes.
   - AT-5: Karpathy section removed.
   - AT-7: delta paragraph removed from SKILL.md and the system prompt.
   - AT-8: "look for what the review did not" removed.
   - The same pattern in `arms-report.bats` lines 65 and 115 does work, because those are last lines.

5. `head/evals/tests/arms-report.bats:132-139` — **AR-6 does not test what its title says.** The title claims "the default output path is evals/results/arms-report-<date>.md under the results root's repo", but every call passes `--out` or fails validation, so the default is never checked. The claim is also wrong: `report.sh:55` puts the file under the script's repo root, not the results root's.

6. `head/evals/tests/run-arms.bats:40,58` with `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:171` — **RA-1's "without a … CLI call" check is blind.** The dry run calls `write_manifest`, which runs `"$claude_bin" --version`, so the real CLI is executed. The test's `[ ! -e "$T/argv" ]` cannot see this, because `claude-stub.sh:20` exits on `--version` before writing `STUB_ARGV_FILE` (line 43).

**run-arms.sh behaviour**

7. `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251-257,265,408` — **Re-running an existing batch duplicates results.** A re-run with the same source and model is allowed. It rewrites MANIFEST and STATUS (counters restart at 0) but appends to `<arm>/results.jsonl` (`>>`), with no resume or dedupe.
   - STATUS then reports e.g. `trials_done: 9` while results.jsonl holds 18 rows with repeated trial numbers.
   - Error rows from an earlier partial run stay and are counted by arms-report, even when the batch now reads `complete`.
   - Duplicate trial numbers merge in `trial_means` and inflate coverage counts.

8. `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:246` — **Interrupting a batch leaves executors running (from reading only, not run).** `cleanup` kills only the `jobs -p` PIDs, which are the background `run_trial` subshells. The running `execute-agent.sh` / `timeout claude …` children are not signalled, so after an interrupt or a drift `exit 3` they keep running, unsupervised, and their sandboxes are never destroyed.

All work was read-only; scratch copies under /tmp and $HOME were removed and /workspace/pr is unchanged.

    base_min = min(base_tm.values()) if base_tm else None

            else:

#   LOA_EVAL_ARM          arm id (default baseline). Setting it at all is "arm
#                         mode": the prompt tree's .loa.config.yaml is also
#                         materialised so every arm sees the same config.
#   LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES  JSON object {toggle: false, …}; when unset the arm is
#                         resolved from LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, else from
#                         evals/suites/<task dir name>.yaml (`ab.arms[]`)
#   LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT  recorded as source_commit (default: the prompt
#                         tree's HEAD)
#   Toggles are applied to the SANDBOX COPY only, after every materialisation
#   step and immediately before the executor starts; each is verified absent

head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39 — FS-2 never checks anything: the jq filter defines `m($r)` using `$in`, but `$in` is only bound after the def (`. as $in | ...`), so jq rejects the program ("$in is not defined", 2 compile errors, exit 3). Both sides of the `diff <(...) <(...)` are therefore empty, and the test passes whatever the FR-1.2b/FR-SZ* corpus rows contain. The floor-corpus guard is vacuous. Fix: bind `$in` before the def, or pass the row as a parameter.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:302 — the "change too small to name" escape uses `abs(drop) <= base_spread`. A large negative drop (the arm recalls MORE than baseline) fails that test, so when a recall rule trips (CI upper bound or min-trial) the arm is labelled **recall loss**. The docstring (lines 19-23) says recall loss requires the mean drop to exceed the baseline spread. Line 324's `abs()` likewise reports an improvement as "change named". The pre-registered verdict can invert the result.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:240 — `coverage_gaps` skips every fixture with `planted == 0`, so a clean fixture with 1/3 completed trials raises no coverage gap. Those clean fixtures still feed the refuted-share rule. The docstring (lines 17-18) promises inconclusive when any planned fixture lacks trials_required completed trials.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:30 — the exit-code contract says 1 = refused, 2 = error, but an unreadable or malformed STATUS.json/MANIFEST.json, or a failing yq (`check=True`), raises an uncaught exception and Python exits 1. Callers (report.sh:56) cannot tell a crash from "suite not complete".
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:264 — the `rule_files` toggle succeeds when neither rule file exists: it records "removed: none present" and exits 0, so `no_rule_files` silently runs as baseline (e.g. on a source commit older than the rule files). This contradicts the header promise at lines 63-66 ("a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2; an arm never silently runs as its baseline").
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:271 — `audit_delta_instruction` removes only the first matching paragraph (`_drop_paragraph`) and never checks the sandbox SKILL.md afterwards. If the instruction appears in more than one paragraph, the arm keeps it and still exits 0, although the header (line 64) says each toggle "is verified absent afterwards". Similarly, `companion_voice` (line 243) verifies only `code_review`, not `security_audit`.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:195 — `_drop_md_section` ignores code fences: a `## ` line inside a fenced block in the Karpathy section ends the skip early. Part of the section survives, and the check at line 251 still reports success.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:158 — with LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES set but LOA_EVAL_ARM unset, the toggles are applied yet executor.json records `arm: "baseline"` (line 398). run-eval.sh copies that label into result rows, so a modified run is reported as baseline. Arm mode is also off, so `.loa.config.yaml` is not materialised and companion_voice writes a config holding a single key.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:343 — the comment says every auxiliary model is pinned to the executor model, but only CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is exported. The small/fast helper model is not pinned, and lines 411-413 acknowledge haiku helper calls happen, which undermines the model-skew control between arms.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:408 — re-running an existing batch with the same source and model is allowed (lines 251-256). MANIFEST/STATUS are rewritten with counters reset to 0, but rows are appended (`>>`) to `<arm>/results.jsonl` with no dedupe or resume. STATUS then disagrees with results.jsonl, duplicate trial numbers inflate coverage and trial means, and stale error rows from an earlier partial run are still counted by arms-report.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:246 — `cleanup` kills only the `jobs -p` subshells. The `execute-agent.sh` / `timeout claude` grandchildren are never signalled, so an interrupt or the drift `exit 3` (line 404) leaves executors running unsupervised, with sandboxes never destroyed.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295 — the "not a record fixture; refusing to overwrite" guard fires only when fixture.yaml exists. Any pr-NN directory without one is `shutil.rmtree`'d (line 730). Seeding into pr-01 (the template source) deletes REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md and then crashes with FileNotFoundError at line 745, copying the templates from the directory it just wiped.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312 — binary-rename detection mis-parses git's brace form: `d/{a.png => b.png}` becomes `b.png` and `x/{a => b}/f.png` becomes `b}/f.png`. The binary is not excluded and is copied through `redact()` (errors="replace" decode), producing corrupted files, which breaks the "without binaries" scope (line 33).
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:37 — the header says bridgebuilder labels come from "the Fixed table only", but `parse_findings` (lines 418-460) ignores the file name. Every severity bullet/heading in a bridgebuilder file becomes a label, and a "Fixed" table inside engineer/auditor feedback is parsed too, contrary to the label rule.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:257 — `--approve` demands `--by '<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>'`, but the regex never requires a date, so `--by abc` approves a label file. That approval is what run-arms.sh trusts to admit fixtures.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:160 — the SC-6 "non-record fixture is refused" case never reaches the refusal: its pr-01 has no fixture.yaml, so the seed wipes the directory and dies on a traceback. The test only asserts exit 1 and an absent fixture.yaml, so it passes on the crash and hides the destructive path above.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:90 — `! grep -rqF "$FAKE_KEY" "$C"` is not the last command of the test. Bats/`set -e` ignore `!`-negated commands, so SC-2's headline claim (no secret is written) is never asserted. The same applies to lines 69, 91 and 143.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132 — `! grep -q 'Karpathy' ...` (and line 133) is not the test's last command, so it can never fail. AT-5 does not verify the Karpathy section is gone. The same no-op negation hides the AT-7 checks at lines 152-153 and the AT-8 check at line 166.
head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:126 — `! grep -qE '...T|generated_at' guards.md` is not the last command, so GY-6's "no timestamp in the structural register" assertion is a no-op.
head/evals/tests/run-arms.bats:58 — RA-1's "dry run makes no CLI call" check (`[ ! -e "$T/argv" ]`) is blind: the dry run calls `write_manifest`, which runs `claude --version` (run-arms.sh:171), and claude-stub.sh exits on `--version` before writing STUB_ARGV_FILE.
head/evals/tests/arms-report.bats:132 — AR-6 claims to test the default output path, but every invocation passes `--out` or fails validation, so the default is never exercised. The stated location is also wrong: report.sh:55 resolves it under the script's repo root, not the results root's.
head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-kind-01.yml:25 — the grader regex `[*][*]MEDIUM[*][*].*[Mm]echanical` checks neither the expected citation (`head/.claude/skills/run-status/SKILL.md:13-17` per fixture.yaml) nor polarity. It matches a demoted "**MEDIUM** (speculative…)" observation or "**MEDIUM** … not mechanical", so the task cannot confirm the finding it describes.
head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2 — path-scoping the stash rule to `**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**` and `.claude/hooks/**` ties it to editing shell files. The hazard it documents is running `git stash` via Bash during skill execution, regardless of which file is open. Skill runs and ad-hoc Bash sessions that touch no shell file no longer load the judgment rules the fence cannot express (`stash -k` with pre-commit, fsck before gc).
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 23 findings and a verdict of **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The tracked files under `pr/` are unchanged.

**Merge blockers:**

- **The floor-corpus test checks nothing** (`tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39`). Its jq filter uses `$in` before binding it, so jq won't compile it. Both sides of the diff come out empty and the test always passes. I confirmed this by running the filter.
- **The arms report can call an improvement a "recall loss"** (`evals/harness/arms-report.py:302`). The "change too small to name" check uses `abs(drop)`. So when an arm recalls *more* than baseline and a recall rule trips, it gets labelled recall loss, which contradicts the script's own docstring.
- **The arms report under-checks coverage and confuses crashes with refusals.**
  - Fixtures with no planted defects are skipped by the coverage check, though they still feed the refuted-share rule.
  - A malformed STATUS or MANIFEST file crashes the script with exit 1, the code that means "refused".
- **An arm can silently run as baseline** (`evals/harness/execute-agent.sh`). This breaks the script's stated promise that it never happens.
  - `no_rule_files` succeeds when neither rule file exists.
  - The audit-delta toggle removes only the first matching paragraph and never re-checks the file.
  - The Karpathy-section removal stops early at a `## ` line inside a code block.
  - Toggles set without an arm name are recorded as `baseline`.
- **Re-running a batch duplicates results** (`evals/harness/run-arms.sh`). The status counters restart while rows keep being appended to `results.jsonl`. Separately, interrupting a batch leaves the executor processes running.
- **The corpus seeder wipes directories it should refuse** (`evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh`).
  - Any `pr-NN` directory without a `fixture.yaml` is deleted. Seeding into `pr-01` deletes the template files and then crashes.
  - A renamed binary inside a directory isn't recognised as binary, so it gets copied and corrupted.
  - The bridgebuilder "Fixed table only" rule isn't implemented.
  - `--approve` accepts a name with no date.

**Tests that can't fail:** eleven `! grep …` lines across `seed-corpus.bats`, `arm-toggles.bats` and `guard-yield.bats` aren't the last command in their test. Bats ignores a `!` line that isn't last, so those assertions are never checked.

**Weaker findings:**

- Three other test gaps: RA-1's "no CLI call" check can't see the call, AR-6 never exercises the default output path, and the `review-kind-01` grader regex doesn't check the citation.
- `stash-safety.md` is now scoped to shell files only. The hazard it covers is running `git stash` during any skill run, so it may not load when it's needed. That one is a judgement call.

I read `guard-yield.sh`, the validator kind rule, `loa-status.sh`, `tools/cycle-ratio.sh` and their tests myself. Three background reviewers covered the eval harness, and I re-checked each of their findings against the code before including it. I ran the fence-marker and origin-map checks: the markers match the map rows, and the `floor.yaml` checksum matches its pin.

I couldn't run the full bats suites, because `.claude/settings.json` and some library files aren't in the frozen PR. I also dropped one candidate finding: the new CI step needs `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, which isn't in the PR. The PR's own scope rules leave `grimoires/` out of frozen fixtures, so that file is probably just missing from this snapshot rather than from the change.
